methodology.officialSourcePriority: Official MPSC and district notices, official question papers and final answer keys take precedence.
methodology.frequencyRule: Report topic frequency only from a complete, verified paper sample. methodology.confidence: Confirmed facts are separated from provisional study recommendations. No future-question prediction is made.

verifiedEvidence.fact: MPSC recruitment advertisement for Inspector of Taxes under the Taxation Department is dated 26 April 2017.
An official MPSC result notice confirms that the screening test for the April 2017 recruitment was held on 27 February 2021; the result notice is dated 21 October 2021.

The official MPSC Inspector of Tax Series III booklet records the examination date as 27 February 2021, 150 questions, 300 marks, 2½ hours and no negative marking; it divides the paper into 50 General English, 50 General Knowledge & Aptitude and 50 Mathematics questions.

notVerified: A current post-specific Inspector of Taxes syllabus was not listed on the MPSC syllabus index reviewed on 4 November 2026.
A verified official final answer key for the 27 February 2021 Inspector of Tax booklet was not located in this review; do not attach unverified answer indices.
The 2021 paper is one historical sample from the April 2017 recruitment cycle. It cannot establish recurring multi-year topic frequencies or the pattern of a future recruitment.
provisionalPreparation: Use the historical 50 English + 50 General Knowledge & Aptitude + 50 Mathematics structure for a diagnostic timed mock, not as a guaranteed future pattern.
Practise English error spotting, idioms, word meanings, antonyms, collocations and fill-in-the-blanks.
Revise Meghalaya and Indian General Awareness, polity, history, geography, science, economy, sports and international organisations.
Practise aptitude and mathematics: direction sense, series, averages, ages, ratio, percentages, SI/CI, profit/loss, partnership, work/rate, speed/distance and mensuration.
Study GST/tax administration, constitutional finance and public audit as role-related knowledge; do not assume a separate technical examination section unless the next official syllabus says so.
examTracks.confidence: High confidence in the printed structure of one complete official 2021 paper; insufficient evidence for recurring multi-year topic frequencies or a future examination pattern.

sourceStrategy.gkToday: Use GKToday topic quizzes and articles across history, culture, geography, polity, economy, science, environment, international organisations, books/authors, important days, awards and sports. Write original questions and explanations; do not copy protected wording.
sourceStrategy.crossChecks: Cross-check constitutional, statutory, tax, treaty, standards and time-sensitive facts against primary official sources. Use Meghalaya Government, MPSC and district administration for regional facts. For the 3 November 2026 India S&T Scoreboard item, the PIB launch release and NITI Aayog dashboard are the primary references; no unverified Meghalaya-specific numeric ranking is stated.
sourceStrategy.specialist: Use standard grammar/textbook sources for English, worked solutions for arithmetic/reasoning, official GST Acts/Rules and GST Portal guidance for tax, and authoritative technical references for computer and science.

evidence.fact: Meghalaya became an autonomous State on 2 April 1970 and a full-fledged State on 21 January 1972.
The Sixth Schedule is headed by Articles 244(2) and 275(1) and provides for specified tribal-area administration in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Jowai is the headquarters of West Jaintia Hills and Nongpoh is the headquarters of Ri-Bhoi.
Living root bridges use roots of Ficus trees including Ficus elastica, guided through bamboo or hollowed betel-nut supports.
Wangala is a Garo post-harvest festival associated with Saljong and known as the 100 Drums Festival.
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is on the Tura Range in the Garo Hills and was recognized under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme in 2009.
Khasi and Pnar/Jaintia are classified among the Austroasiatic Khasian languages; linguistic references distinguish them from Garo.
Khasi social organisation is matrilineal, with descent traced through the mother's line; academic research explains the roles of the youngest daughter and maternal uncle.

regionalMeghalayaGK.method: Facts are supported by State and district government sources, the Constitution, UNESCO and academic references. Cultural practices are described with qualifications; promotional tourism labels are not treated as official statistical rankings.
